utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Before we are having the witness, there's one thing I want to mention, that is, this Bench received verification of translation of that document they used during the last witness concerning the translation of a word. I wonder whether both parties have received this memo or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, the Prosecution has. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I want to know the views from parties concerning the submission for -- for admission of this document into the evidence, because we have three, you know, documents, you know, used during the proceedings and at least there are two documents submitted for admission. Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Your Honour, the position of the Defence about is that is that the document that has been produced now, the recent one just provided, accurately reflects the situation and we would be content with that being adduced into evidence and admitted into evidence as an exhibit, noting that it's -- it essentially reflects the -- the opinion that was obtained by the Defence in -- I think it was in May or April of 2004. But -- so yes, pardon me, just in answer to Your Honour's limited question there, that yes, that's our position. Could I just indicate that I don't know if it's -- if Your Honour wants to deal with it now, but there's an issue that arose about how the other ones came into -- into evidence at all, and it may be appropriate to deal with that now, but I note there's a witness here and there's another one waiting, potentially to be reached today. So I'm in the Court's hands. I'm prepared to address the Court about it now, but Ms. Chana is not here and she perhaps ought to be given the chance to respond to what we want to say about that. So I indicate I'm ready, but I'm in the Court's hands about when that's to be dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Re, are you in the position to give me an answer on this question?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, unfortunately, I can't answer that off the top of my head. Perhaps that could await Ms. Chana's next appearance or until Your Honour sets a time to hear submissions on that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe that the best way is to admit one copy of that translation with the memo sent by the CLSS rather than we admit two copies which have some great disputes between the parties. Well, could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your testimony will be finished today. Yes, Mr. Morrissey, please continue your cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Arnautovic. Mr. Arnautovic, I want to now take you to the beginning of your journey down to Herzegovina and in particular to Hrasnica. You indicated yesterday that -- would you just excuse me one moment, please. Yes. Thank you. Sorry. Very well. You indicated yesterday that you were -- that you and your soldiers had to wait for a period at Hrasnica until Ramiz Delalic came and sorted out the issue of the trucks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, I put it to you that, although -- although Ramiz Delalic sorted out the truck, Sefer Halilovic was present at Hrasnica with a journalist called Sevko Hodzic. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see him at all at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. When you left Hrasnica, you did so in the company of Ramiz Delalic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did that with the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And with Ramiz Delalic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But in the convoy with you was Ramiz Delalic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't in the truck with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: My question to you was: In the convoy with you. What's the answer to that?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. You should ask Ramiz Delalic where he was. I know that I was on the truck with the other men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. On your way to -- to Herzegovina, you knew that you might be engaged in combat activities against Croatian people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's the fact that the 9th Brigade had a number of Croatian people in the brigade itself. And I'll give you an example of the -- the chief of military security, Mr. Tomo Juric; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And as far as you were concerned, there was no particular grievance that anyone in the unit held, to your knowledge, against Croats; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. I now take you to Jablanica itself. And I put to you that when you arrived at Jablanica, Ramiz Delalic also arrived there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he remained in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Is it your evidence that he did not go to Jablanica on that morning of the 8th of September? Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He went as far as Konjic, and then he remained in Konjic with Malco Rovcanin and Fikret Kajevic, and then he arrived later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, in the statement that you made on the 3rd of December, 1998 to the cantonal court in Sarajevo - and this is at page 2, Your Honours - did you say this, and this is about ten lines from the top: "I was going into the village of Grabovica, but Rovcanin Malco, Delalic Ramiz, and Kajevic Fikret remained at Jablanica because of additional agreeing with officers of other units that were to take part in the action." Now, did you say that to the cantonal court back in 1998?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recognise the cantonal court because the police and judiciary are all corrupt. They're all saying and writing false things. I do not accept any statements made before those courts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Is it your position that you told the cantonal court in 1998 that Ramiz Delalic and his friends stopped at Konjic and didn't go to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember what I said then and I didn't care, because that was the kind of judge who was intent on locking everybody up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I've just got a question to you about the leadership of the unit that came down to Herzegovina. Now, what you said yesterday is that as far as you knew, Ramiz wasn't originally going to come to Herzegovina as leader at all. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I knew, we were under Zuka's command, and he was not important because somebody else was in command, not him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just focus on my question about Ramiz Delalic, please. Your initial position yesterday was that he wasn't going to come at all; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that. I said he was called to go to Hrasnica. As for Ramiz Delalic, ask him. Call him to testify and he will tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, right at the moment, Mr. Arnautovic, you're here and I'm asking you the questions. The structure of that unit, the assault unit, I put to you, was that the assault unit had a leader who, throughout 1993 and up to the time of this incident, was Malco Rovcanin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Malco Rovcanin was the commander of that assault group up to that time. I don't know when exactly. And then later on there was somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But according to you, Malco Rovcanin stayed with Ramiz on this occasion in Konjic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were on our way there, yes, he stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. So under Malco Rovcanin, there were three platoons or three units, each of which had a leader within the assault company; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many exactly, but I know that from every brigade they all had their own leaders leading the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: We're talking about your unit right now, so just focus on that. In the assault company, there were three platoons, and they were led, I suggest to you, by particular individuals. And I'm asking you now to name those individuals. Who were the three leaders of the platoons within that company of which you were, and had been for a long time, a member?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no platoon leaders. I know there was Zuti, who was then the commander of the assault detachment, and I don't know what his real name is. Zuti was a nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, was Zuti a member of the 9th Brigade or was he from somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a member of the 9th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I want you to just exercise your memory, please, as someone who was the logistics officer for the 9th Brigade assault detachment. What was Zuti's name?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said, I cannot remember his first and last name. I know everybody called him Zuti, because in our part of the world, most people knew each other by nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Well, the situation was this: That when you got to Jablanica, as far as you know, there was no leader of the -- the troops from the 9th Brigade who were going down to Herzegovina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: By the time you got to Jablanica, there was no leader of the 9th Brigade units that were going to Herzegovina; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived in Jablanica, we came to Zuka's headquarters, and they took us over there. We were told we would be staying in Jablanica, not in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But just to deal with my question. When you were taken from Jablanica -- I'll put the question slightly differently, if I'm confusing you. But when you went to -- went from Jablanica to Grabovica, you didn't actually have a leader with you at all, did you?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew what I had to do. I knew what my job was. And I didn't need anyone to command me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But the answer to my question is yes, there was a complete vacuum as far as leadership of the 9th -- of the detachment of the 9th Brigade goes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know because my job was logistics. I just had to do my job. Other people had their own tasks concerning the battlefield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, when -- you've indicated that when you got to Grabovica that some troops had trouble getting accommodation and that they complained to you -- do you remember giving evidence that they complained to you personally, yesterday? Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I was in charge of logistics and they came to tell me they had no accommodation. That's what I said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But were you the leader of these troops who came to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not a leader. I was just an ordinary logistics man.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Are you prepared to put a name on the person who was the leader of your troops - I mean the 9th Brigade troops - in the village of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that Zuti was the leader of that unit that set out toward Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And do you say Zuti was present in Grabovica when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He arrived with us. We all arrived together, except for Delalic, Rovcanin, and Kajevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. All right. And did the troops complain to Zuti that they were being shut out of the houses, according to you?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They complained because I was in charge of logistics. I was taking care of the mattresses and other things. That's why they came to tell me there was no accommodation. They said, "You're in charge of logistics. You see about it."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And -- but according to you, you told them you would go back and talk to Zuka. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I would check to see what was going on and what the problem was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just excuse me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Very well. And is your position this, that you didn't ask Zuti, the command -- your commanding officer at that point, any questions about the accommodation of the troops?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't ask him anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And is there really such a person as Zuti?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is. I see him in Sarajevo daily.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I see. Very well. So what's his name?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zuti.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: How long have you known Zuti?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've known him from the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: 12 years or so; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not 12 years. We met during the war. We would come across each other, say, "Hello. How are you," and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Arnautovic. Now, I want to ask you some questions about what happened when you arrived initially. You've indicated that the troops got out of the -- the trucks or buses. Well, perhaps I should clear that up. Were they buses or trucks that you were in?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By trucks, and there was a jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. With Zuka's man in it; correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His was the jeep. It was brown and white.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And that was the individual called Spaga; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And he was dressed in civilian clothes, including a black leather jacket; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say precisely what he was wearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was he approximately 30 to 40 years old at that time?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He looked as if he was about 35.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Did he have dark hair?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was kind of yellowish.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And did he have with him a Heckler & Koch machine-gun, an automatic gun?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't pay attention to that. That was the free territory where you could move around.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. The fact of the matter is that you were in logistics; is that right? You were a non-combatant by that stage of your career?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to that. That's -- that's actually a legal question under the -- it's capable of legal interpretation according to the laws of war. I think there's probably a better way of expressing what my learned friend is trying to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that without this question you could also ask the follow-up questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may skip this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Arnautovic, is the fact this: You weren't one of the fighters anymore?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I was wounded, I no longer went into combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. It was -- was it your habit or not to carry around an automatic gun? Perhaps I'll ask you the question a bit differently: In the village of Grabovica where the Croat civilians lived, did you carry a Heckler & Koch gun around with you or not?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't need to carry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, when the troops arrived, you had with you Mr. Spaga, one of whose jobs was to take your soldiers to their accommodation -- sorry, I take that back. Don't worry about "your soldiers." You had with you Mr. Spaga, one of whose jobs was to take these soldiers to their accommodation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four or five of them came with us because of the accommodation and they said, "You have the houses here. It's all been agreed with the local people," about accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown P7. It's Exhibit P7.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, having regard to that photograph there, you indicated yesterday where the buses stopped. You'll see that the houses in which 9th Brigade members were accommodated are all very close to where the buses stopped. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you look at the photograph, that's how it seems. But it wasn't all that close.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, it was as close as it seems in the photograph; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was about 150 metres, 50 metres, 100 metres away from house to house, because the houses were scattered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, look, what I'm putting to you is that Spaga and the other soldiers from Zuka's Unit went straight to those houses to put in place the arrangements that had been made. Now, do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The agreement was made earlier. That's what we were told or I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's not what I'm asking you, Mr. Arnautovic, as you well know. Now, what I'm putting to you is that when you were there and in your presence Zuka's soldiers went straight to those houses in order to implement the agreement to accommodate you 9th Brigade troops there. Now, do you agree with that, that's what they did?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. They didn't go to reach any kind of agreement. Everything had already been arranged. They said, "Yes, you can stay there. There are no problems about that."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. So what you're saying is that Zuka's troops, who were there to help you, didn't relay to you or the 9th Brigade any difficulties with these civilians; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't convey to us anything. They didn't say that they had any problems with them, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And looking at that house in the bottom left-hand corner, the big white house, it's your sworn evidence, isn't it, that that had the Solakovic troops in it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And it's also your sworn evidence that it didn't have any civilians in it at the time that you came there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where Solakovic was, I don't know where he was, but I know that his units were there. I didn't see anybody else other than people from his unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And were you aware of the existence of a man called Marinko Maric? Did you ever hear that name while you were in the village?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard of that name, and I didn't know those people there or anything like that. The only thing that I do know: I used to -- actually, I saw those two brothers. They were the only people I saw, those two children.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let me ask you another name, Ante Maric. Do you see the house down in the bottom square there? Do you see it's a divided house, two houses in one? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see this house. This house has been rebuilt. It wasn't like that. It was a little bit different. It was overgrown. It was rebuilt after the war. I don't understand how they were knocked down. When we left the village, all the houses were standing. They were intact. Afterwards they had all been destroyed, after we left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... this, that that house in the bottom left-hand corner was not there when you were there? Is that your position today in court?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This house was there. I am stating that this house was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Well, if evidence is given that the Solakovic troops were accommodated in another house perhaps 200 metres closer to Jablanica, you would dispute that, wouldn't you? And I mean on the 8th of September. You'd dispute that evidence, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not dispute that, because Adnan Solakovic was in that house with some of his people, and once he met Sefer Halilovic there in that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I see. And what date did he meet Sefer Halilovic in that house there?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was -- I can't tell you exactly. It was either the 11th or the 12th, because I remember some of us stayed behind; some of Adnan Solakovic's fighters and this journalist, Sevko Hodzic was there. He was reporting. He said, "Let me take a photo of you," and I took an automatic rifle from Sefer's brother. So we all took these automatic rifles and we had our picture taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. In fact, what I put to you is that there was a meeting days after the killings took place in Grabovica at which Sefer Halilovic attended with Sevko Hodzic and there were other commanders there too, whilst a battle took place down in the Dreznica area. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. I can recall only the things that I do know. I can't tell you what I don't know. I did see Sevko Hodzic there. He said he was a journalist from Oslobodjenje and he was reporting about the progress of the fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you had no difficulty identifying Sefer Halilovic on that occasion, did you? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Identify him in Grabovica, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: On this occasion with Sevko Hodzic in Grabovica. Do you agree with me about -- look, I'll put the question to you because I don't want it to be broken up. Do you agree that on this occasion when you saw Sefer Halilovic with Sevko Hodzic you had no difficulty whatsoever in identifying Sefer Halilovic on that occasion? Correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, because they said, "The commander has arrived," and the fighters knew who he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Mr. Arnautovic, do you agree with this: That in not one single statement, whether it's been made to the cantonal court, the police, or to the ICTY investigators, in not one single statement did you state that Sefer Halilovic was present when Karic made this threat that you allege? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not saying that he was there. Even now I can't remember. I just know what Vehbija Karic said, and he was there for the 4th and the 5th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I want to ask you a question about specific people. I started to ask you this yesterday, and we ran out of time, and now I'm going to put the names to you. Zicro Suljevic, was he there with Karic the day this supposed threat was made?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of them before by their names, but I never actually knew them personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I have to deal with them one by one. Rifat Bilajac, was he present there when Karic made this supposed threat on the 8th of September?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am repeating again, I never met those people personally. I knew Vehbija because he was in Sarajevo. I never met those other people. I don't know who they were. I never met them before. I just know -- or I just knew that they were from the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So Alic, also known as Soko. Was he there on the 8th of September when Karic made this alleged threat?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I am repeating: You can ask me, but I didn't know those people personally. I never met them, other than Vehbija Karic, because I knew him from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Finally, Namik Dzankovic, was he present on the 8th of September when Karic made the alleged threat?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I am repeating what I said. I didn't know him personally. I didn't really pay that much attention to him or the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Arnautovic, I want to ask you a question about this Karic threat that you allege. Did that really happen at all?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the fighters complained, then Karic said -- they were members from different units. They were Croats, they were Serbs, just like we had in our unit. And when they said, "We can't do this. We don't have any accommodation," he said, "What do you mean? Whoever complains about that or doesn't meet -- doesn't help you out, then you can just deal with them summarily."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Since --

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throw them into the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Since you knew Mr. Karic from Sarajevo, you would know that he was a very experienced staff officer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I considered all of those from the ex-JNA as traitors and enemies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Suitable to make a false allegation against perhaps? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These are not false accusations because some of them had fought on the Croat theatre of war, in the Croat theatre of war, and then afterwards they came to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I have to put a lengthy passage to you now, and you'll have to forgive me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would the Court just excuse me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would you just excuse me my delay, Mr. Arnautovic. I apologise for it. Mr. Arnautovic, I have to put a passage to you now, and it's a reasonably lengthy passage. But if I don't give you the whole thing, it won't allow you to understand the question I ask, so I'm going to read it to you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm reading now from the statement made by this witness to the investigators of this Tribunal, and the date of the interview is the 7th of October, 1999, and I'm reading from the third page of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. "When we arrived at Grabovica, we noticed that there were some other military units in Grabovica which had arrived before us. On the other side of the Neretva River there were a lot of the former detainees which had earlier been released from a Croat camp. I think there were about 500 of them on the other side of the river." And I'll stop reading for a moment. Does that accord with your memory so far?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I remember, I never said 5.000. There were about five to six hundred people there from the camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Arnautovic, that's, in fairness to you, precisely what you said in this statement here. You said 500, so ...

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you are saying that I said 5.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, well, I'm reluctant to say that it was a translation issue, but I assure you that you said "500" then, you say "500" now, and I thought I put "500" to you. So we're in furious agreement that it's 500. Okay?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. The interpreter who is interpreting for me, I heard them say "5.000."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, there's no problem. Anyway, I'll press on now. And this is in 1999 you're making this statement: "Ramiz Delalic, Fikret Kajevic, and Malco Rovcanin did not arrive with us at Grabovica because they had to go to Konjic to obtain some ammunition for our soldiers." Now, does that truly state the position?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that they had stayed behind to buy weapons for Sarajevo because there were a lot of weapons there, and that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let me proceed: "At about 9.00 a.m. Vehbija Karic and three to four other high-ranking officers from the General Staff of the Bosnian army arrived at Grabovica. I know that other officers were also from the General Staff because I know them by appearance. Vehbija Karic asked the soldiers how our trip to the place was, what kind of problems we had, what problems we had billeting in the houses." Now, is that all accurate so far?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now I go on: "Vehbija Karic said that there were empty houses in which we could stay and that those -- and that there were houses inhabited by Croat people. He said we could stay with the villagers because everything had been agreed with them beforehand. He also added that soldiers even could wash themselves in the houses because there was water there." Now, is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'll go on: "Other people who had come together with Vehbija Karic also asked us how our trip to Grabovica was, whether we'd had any problems with the trip, whether we had any trouble with -- problems with finding places in which to stay. They confirmed that everything had been agreed to with the owners of the houses and that we could stay with Croat people in their houses and be comfortable." Now, is that all accurate so far?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: "Almost at the same time a lot of the former detainees from the -- from the other side of the river came to us and started asking us to give them something to eat because they had nothing. They also started to tell their stories to soldiers, how Croat soldiers in the camp had tortured them. Their stories were horrible, how Croat soldiers used to use needles and other devices to torture the Muslims in the camp. The former detainees told us that some Muslims had been killed in the camp. We could see ourselves that the former detainees were tortured because some of them only weighed 30 kilogrammes. The former detainees looked terrible." Is that all accurate so far?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: "The former detainees told us that they had not had food for four or five days. They were all very hungry. Our soldiers shared our food with the former detainees we took wish us from Sarajevo for two ready-to-eat, lunch packets each, and we gave those lunch packets to the former detainees. The appearance of the former detainees, the way they looked, affected our soldiers very much. The soldiers became very upset and angry because of what the former detainees told them." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- some people were told what had happened. A lot of things were said by everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of these soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But what you've put in this statement so far that I've read out to you is accurate; correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People got in touch with them. Naturally, they were there and everything. So of course I said that. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. I understand. Now, to go on: "Actual billeting soldiers into the houses started in the evening. I myself with two soldiers occupied an empty house. Those were (redacted) and Nedim Hajric, later he was killed, who were together with me in the same house. A reconnaissance group, commander of which was a commander called Zuti, also occupied an empty house. I think there were about ten soldiers together with Zuti. I didn't know in which -- in what houses other soldiers from our brigade were billeted. I was very tired after the trip. Very soon I went to bed." Now, is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is accurate. But it's not true that we were being billeted during the night. We were being billeted during the day. This did not happen in the evening. I went into a house during the day and not in the evening, as you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Why did you say to the ICTY -- the ICTY investigator that "actual billeting soldiers in the houses started in the evening" if it's not true?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know to whom I said that. I provided the statement once. Then there was this investigator in Sarajevo, Nikolai. He was talking. He thought that he could speak our language, so he was speaking and interpreting. So I don't know how he understood what I said. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But there was present also a proper interpreter called Kanita Halilovic - no relation, I hasten to add of the accused man - is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interpreter was present, but he behaved as if he understood our language and as if he could talk. I mean, he was speaking Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I'll go on: "Next morning Vehbija Karic and the same high-ranking officers from the General Staff came to Grabovica. Vehbija and others officers were staying in front of the house in which I stayed. In front of the house in which I stayed was another house in which soldiers from Adnan Solakovic's units were placed. Soon after the arrival of Vehbija Karic and other high-ranking officers, soldiers from our brigade and other units gathered in the house in which I stayed. I think there were about 100 soldiers in front of the house in which I stayed. I went out of the house and stood at the front. Vehbija Karic asked whether we had any problems, whether we had good rest in the village. Soldiers started to complain. Some of them had to sleep open in the meadow because Croat people of the village had not allowed them to stay in their houses. A lot of soldiers complained. They complained at almost the same period of time. I could say that they said that in one voice. It sounded like the complaint of a crowd. Vehbija said, "You sleep in those houses. If someone protests, throw them right away into the Neretva." Having heard that, I left Grabovica for Jablanica." Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just one thing was left out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Perhaps my friend could just put the little three-word passage between "throw them right away into the river" and where it says "soldiers replied" to make it more accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, of course I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Pardon me. "The soldiers replied, Okay." Now, I think it will be appreciated what the purpose of this question is just the same. Mr. Arnautovic, is that accurate what I've read out, that Vehbija Karic came back the second morning, made a second interview with the soldiers, and it was on the second occasion that he made this comment about throw them into the Neretva to which the soldiers replied, "Okay"?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember very well that Vehbija Karic, when he came, when he said those words, "Throw them summarily into the Neretva River," that's what he said. I don't know how to tell you that in any other words.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You don't have to tell us that in any other words. What I'm asking you to respond to is the question: Is it accurate that Vehbija Karic came back a second time after the soldiers had to sleep out in a meadow and made a complaint about that? Is that accurate or is it not?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember and cannot confirm this. I can remember seeing him once, but I don't remember seeing him twice. It's something that I cannot confirm. This happened six or seven years ago. But I remember that he was there, that he spoke those words, and I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand you stand by that. Could I ask you a question: Have you been told to stand by that?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To me -- nobody said anything to me. I'm just saying what I heard with my own ears and because I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So is the position this: You've got no explanation for the change between your position to the investigator where you've told him there were two visits by Karic and that the threat was made on the second one the following morning after a sleep in the meadow and your current position now, which is that it was in the morning of the very day that you arrived.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigator who was there, Nikolai, made a lot of mistakes and he missed a lot of things with everybody. Perhaps it was some kind of failure on his part or something that he missed or a mistake that he made. It could be anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But, of course, the interpreter, Kanita Halilovic, was there, who did speak Bosnian; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would it give you a terrible shock to know that (redacted) -- I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd seek to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Arnautovic. When Mr. Karic made this supposed threat, you say he'd come down to enquire about accommodation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard him say, "Are you billeted? Is everything all right? Are there any problems?" And that's the way all the soldiers reacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did the soldiers say to him, "Look, go and check for yourself. We can't get in," or words to that effect? In other words, did they invite Mr. Karic to go and look?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People complained. Nobody did anything. I only know that when he said what he said, that they should just summarily be thrown into the river, I don't know if they did anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that particular issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... my question wasn't clear there. It may be the fault of the question. Did the soldiers invite Karic to go and check for himself, to go check?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember hearing anything like that. All I know is that people behaved differently after what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. But just sticking with the question I'm asking, did you say this to the cantonal court in 1998: "By that opportunity, Vehbija asked soldiers how the accommodation was going on, and the soldiers answered that the civilian did not allow accommodation into their houses. Vehbija said that the accommodation was agreed, and the soldiers said to him to go check it, and Vehbija said, 'who opposes to receive you, throw him by short treatment into the Neretva'."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before the witness answers the question, I just asked Your Honours for a policy direction here, and I notice -- recall Your Honours issuing a ruling in relation to the Prosecution's use of statements that were unsigned or weren't -- witnesses who weren't to be called. This particular statement, as I understand it, is an unsigned statement, if my learned friend is referring to the statement of December 1998. It may be, Your Honours, as other Trial Chambers do, take the view that a witness cannot be impeached with an unsigned statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's a very complicated question, and I believe that documents used in the direct examination and the cross-examination are different. In the cross-examination, as in this case, this kind of document could be used because we have no doubt there is a record in that cantonal court, so the reliability of this piece of the document is not in any doubt at all. And the witness has the full right to agree or disagree whatever is written or said in that document, as he did before. So you may proceed, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Because of the delay there, Mr. Arnautovic, I'll read you the passage again and then I'll ask you a question about it. Okay? The passage I want to put to you reads like this -- sorry, I've now lost the page. "By that opportunity, Vehbija asked soldiers how the accommodation was going on, and the soldiers answered that the civilian did not allow accommodation into their houses. Vehbija said that the accommodation was agreed, and soldiers said to him to go check it, and Vehbija said 'whoever opposes to receive you, throw him by short treatment into the Neretva'." Now, I'm focussing on that passage where you said "soldiers said to him to go check it." Now, is that the truth? Is that what soldiers said to him?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I know they told us that accommodation had been agreed. I stand by that. When Vehbija arrived, when they said, "There's no accommodation," and complained, he said, "Throw them summarily into the Neretva." I stand by that. As for that court, I know I didn't spend so much as five minutes there, hardly five minutes, and I have no respect for their methods of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, all right. Well, now I want to ask you some questions about where the individual people were ultimately billeted. Mr. Husic was billeted with you; correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Where was Mr. Mehanovic billeted?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where he was billeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Where was Mr. Malicovic [phoen] billeted?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know these names. I don't know all their names. I know their nicknames.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Where was Musa Hota billeted?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. They were all over the village, in various houses. I came and went. I didn't really pay attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit P3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you see at the -- do you have that picture in front of you now, Mr. Arnautovic?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you see at the left-hand end of the village the tall white house in which you say members of the Solakovic unit were placed?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the left-hand side, yes, and to the right is the one where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. You can see the -- the white house in which you were placed. Very well. In relation to the white house in which you were placed, where was Musa Hota placed?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where he was placed, nor can I say he was here or he was there. One, I didn't pay attention. I didn't go to see them. Whoever needed something would come to the house where I was and be issued with whatever it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Where was Fikret Kajevic based?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fikret Kajevic was in Konjic and Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Hukalic [phoen], where was he based?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. He was somewhere in the village. I don't know exactly in which house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What about Nihad Vlahovljak? Where was he?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give you the same reply for each of them. I really don't know who was in what house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could we go back, please, to P7. Do you have that photograph?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you see the brown house directly in the middle left of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Who was in that house?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Our soldiers were there, five or six of them, but I can't remember exactly who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, that's 50 metres from your house, and I'd ask you to exercise your memory, please. Who was there?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall because I didn't go round the village. I just went to the house and I went back and forth between Jablanica and Grabovica. I didn't walk around the village and look into the houses to see who was where.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us that you went backwards and forwards several times that afternoon after Karic made his comment. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that you went backwards and forwards several times to Jablanica after Karic made his comment. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came and went. I can't recall now. Too much time has elapsed. But I know well that I came and went.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. When you came back after the first trip, were there still civilians alive in the village that you could see?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first day when I arrived, there were villagers around, civilians. I recall that well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And on the -- but you've indicated that you came and went on a number of occasions. The next time that you came and went on the afternoon of the 8th of September, when you came back to Grabovica after that second trip, were there still civilians alive at that stage?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you precisely. I don't know anything about what happened. Later on I only heard what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But did you see any civilians alive that second time you came back on the afternoon of the 8th of September?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't pay attention. I just remember those two children. And later on I don't remember anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But just stay with the 8th of September at the moment, if you don't mind. On that occasion, is your memory that there were no civilians at all when you came back after your second trip?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you, I didn't pay attention to the civilians. I didn't really look at the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm asking you a more fundamental question, and that is: Were there any civilians at that point?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you again I didn't pay attention. I didn't look to see who was a civilian, who was where and who was doing what.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What clothes was your unit wearing?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were the civilians wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which civilians?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The Croat civilians who were in the village when you arrived.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived, I didn't see them wearing uniforms, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, now I come back to my question: When you came back after the second trip into Jablanica, what was the position? Were there any civilians wandering around not wearing uniform?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the former detainees who were walking around. They were in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When you came back after the third trip, were there any Croat civilians alive at that point, to your observation?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only heard that there were no Croat civilians around when I found those children. As for everything else, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: After you came back to Grabovica the final time, on the evening of the 8th, did you go and sleep in the white house that you've indicated in photograph number 7, P7?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did spend the night there. I went to bed late.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Approximately what time did you arrive in Jablanica that last time? So before you went to bed, how long were you in -- I'm sorry, I misspoke there, so I'll start the question again. When you came back to Grabovica to sleep the night, how long passed before you went to bed?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never looked at my watch, nor did I pay attention to the time. It was wartime. I was concerned with surviving from day to day. I didn't look at my watch and think about the time or wonder what time it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you stay up socialising with people or did you go straight to bed?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was tired. I was exhausted, so I went to sleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I see. And you didn't hear any screaming?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Or any shooting?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was Elvedin Husic with you in that house when you arrived home or not?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was he already there or did he arrive with you?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there in Grabovica. When we arrived and found accommodation, he remained there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But I'm talking about in the white house after you came back from Jablanica for the final time that evening. Was he already there or did he come home a bit later?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there. He and Hajric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did he tell you he'd been out drinking alcohol with any people?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: He didn't mention alcohol?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Ramiz Delalic didn't permit the soldiers to drink alcohol in particular in situations like that, when they were about to go into battle in the next few days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Alcohol was never allowed to be used, either in the barracks or anywhere else. If people left the barracks on leave and went elsewhere, then nobody could control what they were doing, neither he nor anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No. No. But to your understanding, Ramiz would not tolerate drinking alcohol in the village of Grabovica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he would not tolerate it. He would not allow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But the difficulty was, according to you, that Ramiz wasn't actually there, was he?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no problem at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Because you say that as far as you know, there was no drinking; correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about Elvedin Husic, but how do I know whether anyone was drinking or not? I didn't smell their breath to find out whether they'd been drinking. I wasn't competent to monitor whether they were drinking or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, is that an appropriate moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, if you've finished that drinking problems. Yes. We'll have 20 minutes' break and we'll resume at ten minutes to 3.00, I think -- right? To 4.00. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Pardon me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Arnautovic. I now want to take you to the 9th of September. What time did you wake up in the morning of the 9th of September, that is, the day after you arrived.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the morning. It might have been around 8.00, but I can't be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And did you then make two more trips in to Jablanica and back again?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went to Jablanica and back, and then I went to Jablanica and stayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, about what time did you come back to Grabovica after that first trip in to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what time it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, let's try to get an estimate as best you can. You woke up approximately 8.00 -- I understand you're not specifying exactly 8.00. You woke up at approximately 8.00. And I take it you then got up, had breakfast; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't really breakfast. I can't normally eat breakfast.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Did you have a coffee in the morning before you left?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The first thing I do is take something sweet and then light a cigarette.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, on this -- on this occasion, did you wake up in the white house and take something sweet and light a cigarette?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the white house, I woke up, in the house I mentioned, and I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. That's okay. You had a sweet and a cigarette; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've been doing that ever since I started smoking when I was ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And Elvedin Husic was right there with you at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was there. I didn't pay attention to whether he was asleep or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you receive a visit from a man named Lujinovic [phoen], Sulejman?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you know the man I'm talking about, Mr. Lujinovic?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember many of the men. A long time has gone by. Some of them have been killed. In fact, a lot of them have been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did Mr. Lujinovic come in to the white house and tell you and Husic that something bad had happened?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that. I don't remember anybody coming and saying something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: See, according to you, you got quite a shock on the following day, the 10th, when you heard the story of the boys and realised that some crimes might have been committed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I heard from the boys, when I heard what they said, that's when I learned everything that had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. So that after your coffee and your sweet, did you then drive in to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you drive in a jeep that had been lent to you by Zuka's Units?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I know I was driving around in that jeep and there was another car. I don't remember what it was called. I remember well that the jeep was brown and white. It had a white roof and it had -- it was brown on the sides and it used petrol.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When you're speaking of this other car, you're not speaking of any car associated with Ramiz Delalic, are you?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Ask him. He wasn't there until those children turned up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. That's okay. So what you say is that -- well, just a moment. When you referred to another car just a moment ago, are you talking about a car associated with Mr. Delalic or are you talking about some different car?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not talking about any car that had anything to do with Ramiz Delalic, because he didn't come to Grabovica until those children were found.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. So now I'll come back to the question: Which vehicle did you drive in to Jablanica when you went in this morning of the 9th?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember what vehicle it was or what its name was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And did you there collect some lunch packets to be distributed among the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from Zuka's base, from the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Are these lunch packets, are they in small metal containers?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were -- I don't know. These were the best-packed lunches. They -- they were about 100 of such packets. But they contained everything, these meals.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. And you brought those back to Grabovica; is that correct? In the vehicle, whichever one it was?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I brought the lunch packets. I remember it well that they were brought in this brown-white jeep. It was quite big and you could fit a lot of things in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And when you brought back those lunch packets and arrived in Grabovica, approximately what time was it?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what time it was. I didn't really pay attention to the time. It was war, so I wasn't really that aware of what time it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, even so, I'm going to see if we can arrive at an estimate. Did you leave Grabovica at about -- approximately - and I understand you can't be precise - but approximately half past 8.00 in order to go in to Jablanica to get the lunches?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really tell you precisely. I really don't know. I wasn't paying attention to the time. I know that most of the people were asleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. Well, when you say most of them were asleep, what you mean is no one seemed to be moving. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was leaving, there were some soldiers walking around, but one didn't really pay attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. It took you about 15 minutes, I suggest, to cover the distance between Grabovica and Jablanica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I couldn't tell you. It depends on the kind of driving involved. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just think back to this. You were driving along a relatively well-sealed road and you were not under fire and you were in a jeep. Now, do you agree that it took about 10 to 15 minutes to drive that distance?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not 10 to 15 minutes, because I don't really enjoy speeding or fast driving because why do I want to get hit with a bullet? Why would I want to crash into the Neretva?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: If the evidence otherwise proves that the distance between Jablanica and Grabovica is about 12 to 13 k's, can you indicate approximately how long it actually did take you - you being the man in the car who drove this distance - to cover that distance?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm driving in a normal pace without speeding, I would need about 20 minutes. If I were going 80 kilometres per hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, I understand it's unfair to press you to be precise about those speeds, but it's fair to say this, isn't it, that you would have been in Jablanica by half an hour at the most? Correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't need a half an hour to reach Zuka's headquarters. With normal driving, you can reach it in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And did you drive at a speed that was basically normal speed on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At a normal speed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. At Zuka's base, how long did it take you to load up the lunch packets?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed there -- sometimes you would stay there. There was a coffee bar there next to the headquarters. You'd have coffee, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So on this occasion -- we'll take it step by step. How long did it take to load up the -- the lunch packets? Was that a 10-minute job or a 15-minute job?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there are more people there you could load it up in five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And after you -- and is that what happened on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean what happened?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is: On this occasion when you loaded up the lunch packets, did it take you about five minutes, given the help that you got?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will only tell you one thing: I didn't look at the time. I wasn't paying attention to the time, and I wasn't in a hurry. There was no need for me to pay attention to the time. So it took as long as it took. I won't answer any more such questions because I'm not in a race or anything. If you look at your questions, it would seem that -- as if I knew something, but I wasn't really -- there was no need for me to hurry up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just bear with me, please, Mr. Arnautovic. After you'd loaded up the packages, did you stop and have a cup of coffee?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember specifically. I went back and forth to Jablanica on that day a few times, and then I stayed, and then the next day I saw those two children. I really don't remember what I had for lunch yesterday, never mind about something that happened 13 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. But just stick with the questions. After you had loaded up the -- the lunches and possibly had a cup of coffee, you drove back to Grabovica, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would -- went back and forth. That's what happened, like I said it. I went back and forth two or three times and then I spent that night in Jablanica. I stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And when you came back after this first trip on the morning of the 9th, you arrived back in Jablanica -- back in Grabovica, I'm sorry, you came back to Grabovica no more than one hour after you set out; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying again I didn't pay attention to the time, so I can't really reply to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, do you agree that it would have been no more than two hours after you left?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really answer to any time-related questions. I really wasn't thinking in terms of time. I wasn't paying attention to that. I wasn't really interested how much time I needed for what. There was no need for me to be in a hurry. There was no -- there were no actions going on at that time so that there would be a need to rush in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's what we are asking you about, Mr. Arnautovic. When you came back to the village, I put it to you positively that you had been away for a maximum period of two hours. Now, do you disagree with that? Do you say you would have been away for longer than two hours?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying again I can't really look at it from the time point of view. I wasn't paying attention to that. I really don't know how long it took, and I'm repeating this again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But you were back in that village after the first trip by the middle of the morning; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the middle of the morning? I don't know what that means to you, the middle of the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You tell me what it means to you, "the middle of the morning."

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to me, "morning" is in the morning, at 7.00. When it gets light, then it's morning. Because we would express that maybe in different terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you distribute any of those lunches to the soldiers when you got back?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I left it at the house where I was staying because that young man Hajric was there to help out, to look after that, to give them out, and I had one book where I was keeping records of what was given to whom by first and last name. But then during the arrest and review of the documents, that book disappeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Arnautovic, some people have given evidence in this court about killings that were going on in the village at that time. But what you're saying is that when you were there, you saw no signs of any killings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No signs on that day. There were no signs that there were any killings or that anything happened. And there was no talk amongst the soldiers either, because you would have heard something. That's what soldiers are like, our soldiers, and people are like that as well. There would always be some talk about something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You say there wasn't any; correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on that day. Nobody said anything. You couldn't hear anything. There were no whispers or anything like that. Until -- right until the time that those children were found.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And you can give that evidence in this court because you spoke to some of the other soldiers; correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not some other soldiers. Soldiers who had been staying there. I don't know what you mean "others." It's all the same. It was all the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Tell us the names of some of the people that you spoke to on the 9th of September in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't speak to anybody on the 9th of September in the evening because I wasn't there that evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm --

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And during the day, it was just in passing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And which people was it you spoke to just in passing during the day?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was this young man Hajric, there was Husic. Perhaps one of them would have said something had anything happened. Nobody mentioned anything. Nobody said anything. Nothing happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you've mentioned Husic. You knew Husic quite well, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were in the unit together, in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But a bit more than that. You were friends with Husic then, as you are now; is that correct? Well, I'll break it up. You were friends with him then; correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't before. Only when we knew each other during the war. Before the war, I had some other friends, different friends, and life was different, in the same way that my life is different now. So I have a different life now and different friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In September of 1993, you were friends with Mr. Husic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were all friends. We were all one. Everyone fought for everybody else, fought, died, and saved others. Nobody left anyone behind. Not a wounded man or a killed man was left behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, Mr. Husic was also good friends with another man called Mr. Mehanovic in September of 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am telling you now, we were all friends. We were all one. A bullet waited for each one of us. Each one of us had the same fate. We were all the same. There was no question of a person -- this or that person being a friend. A friend is something different. A friend is something special.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you know Musa Hota?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. He was there in the brigade, in our brigade. Actually, he came from a different brigade. He was transferred to our brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did he arrive in your brigade on or about the 15th of July in 1993?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he arrived in 1993, but I don't know exactly when that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
