utterances.text: But it was only a matter of one or two months before this operation took place. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think it was thereabouts. Perhaps he came over for two or three months. I just know that he was transferred. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. He was a pretty tough guy, wasn't he, Mr. Hota?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends on who is forming this opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, what's your opinion?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a pretty big fool. I could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But he was a big, strong fighter with a bad, bad temper; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There was talk of all sorts in Sarajevo. But as far as every person was concerned, each person was a good fighter. Some of them had -- some people had a good opinion of him and some of them praised him. Some of them criticised him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'm just asking you to be limited to what you actually saw yourself. And the question is: Did you see whether he behaved himself properly when Ramiz Delalic was around?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When do you mean, when he was around? Are you talking about Grabovica or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm not trying to trick you in relation to Ramiz and Grabovica. I'm just asking you generally speaking what you observed of Musa Hota is that when he was in the company of Ramiz Delalic, then he would behave himself properly. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not him. Everybody had to behave properly when they were in the barracks. As far as behaviour outside of the barracks, that is something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I see. Did you see the man -- during your trips on the 9th, did you see the man you've -- whose name you don't remember who had the nickname Zuti on any occasion?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was present when Ramiz lined up the soldiers, when he lined up -- assembled the unit. So that he could see if the children would recognise anyone or identify anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did he get a special yelling-at by Ramiz on that occasion of the line-up because these things had happened when he was supposed to be in command or not?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no need for him to be yelled at because the children said that the people that they had seen personally were not actually in the line-up, because there could be no greater accusation that could be made against anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, no. But I take it you agree with the proposition that Ramiz Delalic did not single out this man Zuti for any specific criticism on the day when Ramiz ended up coming to Grabovica and lining up the soldiers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ramiz had no reason to criticise him, because it was not known who did that; was it our people, who was it who did that. Nobody knew who did it and what they did, so we don't know if it was any of our people or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand that. Now, returning to the 9th, where we were, in your trips to and from the village, did you see any old Croatian villagers walking down the road towards Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There were refugees around, and I saw them. There were those who had been in the camps. They were passing by, walking around. But I can't really say whether they were Croats or Muslims or whether it was a former inmate or something. I really didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When lunchtime came on the 9th, to your knowledge were those lunch packets distributed or not?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no specific lunchtime with us. People ate whenever they had time to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, were those lunch packets distributed during the day of the 9th?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each fighter could take his two lunch packets, because that was the daily ration, two lunch packets. So they could take them whenever they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown P3 once again, photograph number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would you just look to the right -- I just want you to focus on the white house in which you had stayed. Do you see that house?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And the trees immediately to the right of that -- of that house can be glimpsed two buildings. The second of them is hidden behind the blue woodsmoke that can be seen and the first of them can be glimpsed. Do you see those two houses indicated by two greyish-white dots within the trees?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see a sort of dot there, and then something else over there, where there is smoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Do you recall a base being established for your unit of the 9th Brigade in either of those buildings in the trees on the 9th of September?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that, because there is a sort of field, a clearing next to this house, and I see it now here, but when I was there, I didn't really pay attention to that. But I know to the left of the white house there was a field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When you say "to the left of the white house," do you mean as you stand in the door of the white house and look out towards the Neretva River?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I'm standing at the door, it's to the left. Now as I look at it, the field is on the right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. What you mean is on the side nearest to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. The field is to the right of this white house where these bushes are. I don't know what you want me to say here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No. No. I just want to make sure that we're referring to the same direction. Looking at the photograph, the field is to the right of the white house; correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, behind this wood. Behind these trees is the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And to the right of that field are the two buildings that you've noted earlier; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it here, where there is smoke and there is also some sort of spot or point there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you go to those buildings approximately -- at approximately evening-time as the sun went down on the evening of the 9th of September?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You're in a position yourself to say that Ramiz Delalic did not go there at that time either, aren't you? Because you were with him in Jablanica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Jablanica on the 9th in the evening with Ramiz Delalic, Fikret Kajevic, and Malco.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. So according to you, Ramiz Delalic, who is also known as Celo, could not have been in those buildings there at evening-time on the 9th of September. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ramiz Delalic only appeared when those children were found. Before that, he didn't come and he wasn't staying in this place, Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And did you ever see any livestock gathered at those buildings in the woods there, the ones we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see it in the woods, but I know that there was some livestock up in the hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, we're not disputing with you about that. It's a question of timing though, Mr. Arnautovic. Did you notice any soldiers driving calfs or goats towards that part of the village where those -- those buildings are?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. Nothing. I noticed nothing. I was going back and forth, so I really can't say what was going on during the day because I was going back and forth. I cannot say that there was any shooting. I didn't hear any. When I was there, I didn't hear any. I don't know if there was any shooting when I was away. And as far as that's concerned, I really can't say anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: On the evening of the 9th, when you say you met Ramiz Delalic in Jablanica, where precisely did you meet him? Was it in a cafe or a hotel or was it at Zuka's base? Where was it?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was Zuka's base, where the coffee bar was, and there were two rooms behind where there was a sort of command headquarters, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And where was it that you met with Ramiz Delalic on that occasion on the evening of the 9th?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There, at Zuka's headquarters. Not in the evening though. I came before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What time did you come? Approximately what time did you come?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could still see when I arrived. It was still daytime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And was it getting dark in that part of Herzegovina at approximately 6.00 in those days?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't get dark at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: At what time did it get dark?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, it would get dark at around 8.00, because I know. I go to the mosque, so I can tell what all the different times of the day are. Aksam is actually the very early twilight.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And is that the time that you arrived back?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't Aksam time. This was between -- it was still perhaps two hours to go before Aksam.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You indicated that on that occasion you saw Ramiz and also Zuka and also Sefer Halilovic. You indicated that to the Prosecutor. Did you see Sefer Halilovic's son on that occasion, a 12-year-old boy?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was around there with him. I know that he was staying with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you see him on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And on this occasion, did Ramiz take the opportunity to ask you whether the accommodation problems had resolved themselves?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because as I said -- I said it was -- I took a sponge -- I took a mattress from Zuka's headquarters, and I said that there was no problem for the fighters to be billeted. They had sleeping bags and sort of foam mattresses. That's -- that's what they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you see whether Zuka and Celo left the village of -- or left Zuka's base and drove anywhere in the evening of the 9th --

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't drive off anywhere. They had -- they stayed there the whole night, almost until morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: How is it that you're able to say that with confidence?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there were preparations underway for the action. Agreements were being reached, consultations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, what you've said -- I think your evidence yesterday is that after sleeping in Jablanica, you then on the following morning, the morning of the 10th, returned to Grabovica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I set out on that morning together with Ramiz Delalic to tell them about the action, to tell them to get ready for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So what your account is is that it was you together with Mr. Delalic who drove from Jablanica back to Grabovica; correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you drove in the car or the -- or the jeep in which you had travelled the previous night in to Jablanica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The jeep, the brown-and-white one, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And in that brown-and-white jeep, you say you and -- and Ramiz came back to the village and there encountered the two boys; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I just want you to assist me with a matter here, Mr. Arnautovic. Back in 1998 at the cantonal court --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm referring now, Your Honours, to the statement of -- provided to us by the Prosecutor to the cantonal court dated 3rd of December, 1998, and I'm referring to the third page of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Out of fairness to the witness, perhaps he could be provided with a copy of the statement if extracts are going to be read to him so that he could actually see what's being read to him in context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it depends on how long that part --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, this is not like the previous one. It's a short one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's try that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. If there's any difficulty, of course the Prosecutor can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would you please read slowly. The interpreters do not have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've been requested to read slowly, which I will comply with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The quote begins like this, Mr. Arnautovic: "Tomorrow after staying for the night at Jablanica, I returned again in to Grabovica among soldiers and by that opportunity I found two children at entrance into village who came before the car I drove." I'll just stop for a moment there. There's then a passage concerning what you were told by the children. And then you go on in this way: "About these events at Grabovica, I heard first from children I met. I did not see any corpse and returned immediately to Jablanica to inform Delalic Ramiz hat I heard from children." I'm going to read two more sentences: "I left the children with soldiers and did not take them along to Jablanica. I know that Ramiz Delalic after this returned immediately to Grabovica from Jablanica, that is, he came with me and talked with the children." Now, Mr. Arnautovic, that's quite different to the story that you're telling today, isn't it? Because there you're saying that you came by yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, I object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The first proposition my learned friend has to establish is in fact that the witness said this at the cantonal court and it in fact was recorded accurately what he said. It is only after the witness has agreed with that that he can then put to him it is in fact a prior inconsistent statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not being put as a prior inconsistent statement yet. It's just being put that it's different. And we'll see what happens after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, that's not what he said though. He said that, you said because you're saying there that you came by yourself. That's very different. That's accepting that he actually said that, as opposed to something that is recorded. They are two completely different propositions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe we could ask the witness to make comments on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Arnautovic, that's what you said to the cantonal court, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that to the cantonal court, because that court, as I've already said, is a court I don't recognise. Because the police, the army, they are all connected with it, and they want to destroy Ramiz Delalic. They want to shift the blame onto him. I spent only five minutes in that court and then I left that office. I simply didn't want to talk to the judge about certain things. And the only thing that I stand by is what I say before this court, because in Bosnia all the authorities are corrupt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, not the Minister of -- the Ministry of the Interior aren't corrupt, are they, Mr. Arnautovic?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, it is. It certainly is. It's corrupt. Everybody in Sarajevo knows. We know a lot of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What about Bakir Alispahic? He wasn't corrupt, was he?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you tell me whether he's corrupt or not. When the war started, that man didn't have a loaf of bread to eat, and now he has tens of thousands of marks, so you tell me whether he's corrupt or not. You think about it a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I'm just asking you. Why is it that you say Bakir Alispahic is corrupt?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object. I should have objected before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: But I object now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And I ask that that last be struck from the record. It's irrelevant to the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think you have a reason. I think you have a reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I won't persist with that question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Arnautovic, nevertheless, did you sign the record of the witness here in -- in which you participated at the cantonal court on December the 3rd, 1998? Did you sign it?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I won't tell you I didn't sign it. I did only because I wanted to leave that office as soon as possible. It was Ramadan. It was a fast. It's stupid to be invited before a court during Ramadan when you're fasting. A fast is something special in Islam, among Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But it's important to tell the truth as well, isn't it, Mr. Arnautovic?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, when we were all arrested, people were threatened with shooting. They said they had specialists that could flay them alive. They used all kinds of methods.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then people were afraid and said whatever they wanted them to say. There are some that went crazy after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Arnautovic, don't misunderstand the questions here. In the statement that you gave -- the statement that I put to you that you gave to the cantonal court, what you seem to say is that Ramiz Delalic was indeed in Jablanica that night. What I'll do is I'll read parts of it to you and you tell me if it's true.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ramiz Delalic was in Jablanica that night, and I was together with him when we found that child. And if our Prosecutor says that I was there on my own when we found the child, that's their problem. I didn't even read that statement. I simply wasn't interested in that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I call for the production of the original of that statement, if it's present in court, in the hands of the Prosecutor. And I mean the Bosnian original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- yes, do you have it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I've unfortunately left mine in my office. I was just going to ask our case manager to get an investigator to bring it down. But I believe the witness possibly has a copy in B/C/S with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Mr. Morrissey, I -- I think the question is quite clear on that, you know. No matter whether you show this, you know, record to the witness or not, we see some, you know, discrepancy between the two. I think you have achieved your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the Court pleases. Yes. Well, now, just excuse me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Arnautovic, I want to put a different account to you now. And this one, Your Honour, I'm reading from the ICTY investigator's statement dated 7 October 1999, and I'm reading from page 4 of that statement. I'm going to read out a passage. It's got a -- it's got a few sentences in it. So listen carefully and then I'll ask you some questions at the end. It's about seven or eight lines long, Your Honour. "Four of us, that is Ramiz Delalic, Malco Rovcanin, Fikret Kajevic and myself, stayed in the Zulfikar base until next morning. The next morning at about 6.00, the four of us, Delalic, Rovcanin, Kajevic and myself left the Zuka's base for Grabovica. We stayed at the same empty house in Grabovica in which I slept the first night after our arrival at Grabovica. Ramiz asked me to wake him up at 10.00 since he had to have a meeting at the Zulfikar base. I also went to sleep because I was tired. I woke Ramiz up about 10.00 a.m. Ramiz and myself went to the Zuka's base in the car jeep. At the exit from Grabovica, we were stopped by five or six soldiers. Three or four were from our brigade and two others were from other units. Now I cannot recall their names. The soldiers told us that they had found two Croat children, two brothers, in the forest." Now I have some questions for you about that passage. First of all, you agree that that passage tells a different story to that which you have given in court yesterday and today; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for what you've just read, first of all, I never said "we went" nor was Grbavica mentioned. Grbavica is in Sarajevo. I was not in Grbavica. The Chetniks were in Grbavica. Five or six times you said "Grbavica. You were in Grbavica with Rovcanin and Delalic." And I don't understand how this was written. If this is what Nikolai was doing, I'm simply not interested. This man thought he knew our language, when in fact he didn't know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But once again, you agree that Kanita Halilovic, the translator, was there at all times during this interview?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she was there. But it was he who asked questions and talked to me in our language, the Bosnian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, is your position this: That you simply never said that? Is that what you say?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that. You mentioned Grbavica five or six times. Grbavica is not Grabovica. There's a huge difference. Otherwise, I would have been a Chetnik. It will turn out I was a spy with Delalic and the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, is it the truth that you came back to Grabovica and slept for four hours early in the morning of the 10th of September or not?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything. I don't know what to tell you. I abide by what I said before this Tribunal. That's how it is. I met up with Ramiz Delalic and then when we met those children, he lined up the troops. And as for what Vehbija said, I stand by that. And now you're talking about Grbavica. That's enough to prove how many mistakes there are in that statement and how Nikolai put questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you know how it is that you came to be so unlucky that two different sets of -- of statement takers on two different occasions have come up with two different false versions?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, I object to this. I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- the line of questioning my learned friend is putting to the witness it's clearly unfair if you look at the extract which is read. The statement is clearly -- clearly has to be wrong because in that same passage it says that he stayed at Zuka's base on that same night and at Grabovica on the same night and woke up in both places on the same night. There's clearly an error in the statement in the way it's been taken. Proofing notes we gave to my learned friend told him the witness said it was incorrect the way it was taken, and it's clearly apparent on the face of it that there is something wrong in -- in the way that it is written. He cannot have stayed in both places on the same night and woken up in both places on the same night. My friend knows that and it's unfair to put it to the witness in that sense without giving him the statement to read and allowing the witness to go back and to see the chronology there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll have to respond to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Because that went outside of what's a proper objection, and I can respond to it. Does the Court have in its -- I don't know what the position is with the e-court. Do you have in possession that statement? Because I'll take the Court to it in detail and indicate that there's nothing necessarily contradictory about it at all. Effectively what I submit the statement says is that they stayed in Jablanica, the four who are being referred to -- stayed in Jablanica but then at 6.00 a.m. drove down to Grabovica and had a sleep for four hours. There is nothing internally incoherent about that statement at all. My learned friend says that I know different. The Court may draw its own conclusion if you need to engage in what counsel knows, generally speaking a barren exercise. But nevertheless the statement does not contain the inherent error that my learned friend points out. If he sees fit to point it out while the witness is sitting listening, that's a matter for him. In any event, the same situation obtains as obtained with the last thing that I put to him. He doesn't adopt this as his own words. He doesn't agree that he said that at all, and it places me in the position of relying on it for a limited purpose only, and that is as a prior inconsistent statement rather than one which he's adopted as being the truth because I can't claim that he has. He hasn't. Nevertheless, I put it to him. He's said what he has to say about it. If there's any apparent unfairness I'm happy to correct it, but the one that has been identified is not an unfairness in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe at my hands we have the witness statement, and I believe that you have made your point very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So would you please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: With the greatest pleasure and gratitude. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, you've already answered questions about --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to commence a topic. I haven't kept an eye on the time. And so I'm in the Court's hands. If you indicate that it's time for a break, I'm about to commence a new topic now, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we will take a break at 15 minutes past 5.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, as the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And could I ask you how long are you going to take?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Oh, I'm going to make an effort to finish by that time. It may be that I can finish by that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, try you best.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Because we have another witness, you know, waiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, as the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, you -- I'd now ask the witness once again to be shown P3. And I'd like the witness to be given the assistance of the pen, if that's possible. Could you please mark where it was that you met the soldiers who told you about the two boys.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We met them -- I can't see because of the bushes, but it was around here. There was a barrier and there was a house, but I can't see that very clearly now because there's a lot of bushes there. There was a house and near it there was a barrier put up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Who was manning -- now, sorry, pardon me. I understand what you say, Mr. Arnautovic. Is that mark there an -- is that accurate as to where it was, or would you like to see a photograph of the road a little further up?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know where this house was. I don't know how to say. It was a sort of stone house. And then there was a barrier there, and that's where you entered Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Could I just ask that the witness be shown P79 -- or perhaps, sorry. I stop there. I offer that for tender at this point as marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It is admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Defence Exhibit D172, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Yes, could the witness please be shown P79.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have in front of you now a photograph that's got various yellow arrows drawn on it?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm not sure that the witness has the -- has the right photograph in front of him.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It has the numbers in the top right-hand corner 01494686.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the situation is -- is technologically difficult, I might try another -- I'll try another approach. I apologise to all concerned. If it's nearly there, I'll wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have the picture now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And my apology, Mr. Arnautovic, for keeping you waiting like that. Now, does that picture there allow you to do any better in terms of where you met the soldiers who told you about the children in the first place?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can see here now, these are recently built buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Could I just -- you'll see that there are some long low buildings along the road which are recent sawmills. Do you see those?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember when we were entering Grabovica the road was straight and there was a barrier put up, and I think it's near the house marked "14."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But there was no bend in the road. The road was completely straight.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I think in fairness to you, Mr. Arnautovic, the road still is straight and that's just a bend that -- that's just a path that goes up to the road. But in any event, could you mark as best you can with the blue pen on that map approximately where you met those soldiers.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you enter the village of Grabovica, it was the first house on the right, the first house. I can't be completely sure now whether this is the house, because later on this was destroyed. Everything was destroyed. But I think this should be it. If that's the stone house, that was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Can you remember which soldiers were -- which, if any, soldiers were living in that house at that time?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I note Crni was there, the man called Crni.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Is that Mr. Turkovic?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know his name. I know only his nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Can you remember who else was living in that house, please?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall exactly who was there. I know Crni was there and there was a barrier there and the soldiers manning the barrier changed. They changed shifts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And which unit were those soldiers from?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. They were mixed. There were probably shifts. I don't know how it worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were there any 9th Brigade soldiers amongst those manning that barrier?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was Crni there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Any others? Any other 9th Brigaders, I mean.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Is that --

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't pay all that much attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. I understand that. Is that the same spot at which you first saw the children themselves, or did you see them somewhere else first?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I saw them there when I arrived with Ramiz.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. So this photograph depicts the spot that you've marked where both the soldiers and the kids were; correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said Crni was there. I didn't say the soldiers. I only saw Crni.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And the children?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the children. They were there with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I tender -- well, I offer that for tender as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Defence Exhibit D173, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, as to the line-up, you've already been asked several questions, and I only have a couple of residual ones. At that line-up when Ramiz asked questions and brought the boys around, you've indicated some of the things that were said by the soldiers and you recall giving that evidence yesterday; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Everybody was saying they didn't know anything, they hadn't seen anything, they hadn't heard anything. That's all I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Not one person there said, "Hey, it's okay. Vehbija Karic gave an order," did they?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they thought, but nobody said anything. All they said was that they didn't know anything, hadn't seen anything, hadn't heard anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Had the story about Vehbija Karic not been invented yet, Mr. Arnautovic?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not an invented story. Vehbija Karic did say that. But the men there said they had not seen or heard anything and they said they didn't know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You said yesterday that Musa Hota was missing from that line-up. Did you point out to Ramiz Delalic that Musa Hota was missing?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five or six fighters were missing because allegedly they had gone to do reconnaissance because an action was being planned. I didn't say, "Musa Hota is missing" to Ramiz, because I was just an ordinary mortal waiting for a bullet to hit him. I wasn't a commander. I wasn't in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I understand you were a mortal. You had the advantage of being alive at that point though, and that's why I'm asking you the questions about it. And the question is: Why didn't you, having noticed the absence of Hota, draw that to the attention of Ramiz, in whose company you'd been, you say, from the night before? Why didn't you point it out to him?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zuti was there. He was the commander. He should have been the one to take care of all the people. I am not responsible of sending people out into combat or into reconnaissance. It was Zuti's task. So you'd better be asking Zuti about that, because he was the person who was in charge of the men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What about Nihad Vlahovljak? Was he in that line?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. All I know is at the time I noticed that Musa wasn't there and a few people, other people who were scouts, but nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. I'm not going to revisit the questions about what happened back in Jablanica with the boys. I want to ask you a question now about when you came back to Grabovica. After the boys were taken to Jablanica and left there, did you come back and search the village for bodies?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People came back to the village. There were people who kept coming back to the village. Nobody saw anything. Nobody found anything. No dead bodies were found. No one found anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But did you join in a search for such dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's nothing to search for. If they're not there nearby, then there's no other place to look for them. Where could they have disappeared? If somebody were to have taken the bodies away out further, then in my opinion that whole thing would need to be organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you look for any digging, any signs of digging?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't pay attention to that. I simply didn't even believe that something like that could have happened that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Even today are you participating in a cover-up of what really happened there, Mr. Arnautovic?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not covering anything up. I cannot say that somebody killed somebody or that I had seen a dead body when I did not. I'm not covering anything up. I am quite certain I didn't see any dead bodies, I didn't see anybody killed. I know that people were killed and I know that these children were found, but I really can't tell you anything other than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown photograph number P79 once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you have that photograph in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the same one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, you've already indicated where the checkpoint was near Crni's house. Did the 9th Brigade set up another checkpoint about 100 metres downstream from that; in other words, 100 metres closer to your white house?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This checkpoint was not set up by the 9th Brigade. That was the first one. After the events, after what happened, after the children were taken in, then there was another checkpoint that Zulfikar set up further up near the bridge Cedo's Wolves were and the Handzar Division were, because they assumed or wanted to prevent anyone else from having access to Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Isn't it nearer to the truth, Mr. Arnautovic, that Zuka set up those checkpoints to keep you and the 9th Brigade in rather than to keep anyone else out?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That checkpoint was set up to prevent access. I know a journalist, a woman, wanted to come in and she was prevented from doing that. I know Bakir Alispahic came with some police units from the direction of Mostar. So when he was coming back, he tried to get in and he was prevented from doing that. And there were some others, perhaps other journalists or people from UNPROFOR who wanted to get in but they were not allowed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When was Bakir Alispahic prevented from getting in, Mr. Arnautovic?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. All I know is that they tried to get in but they wouldn't let them go in. They were prevented. This is what the fighters were saying. They tried to get in and were not allowed to. I was not there to conduct any kind of investigation. I said I was just a mere mortal who was only concerned with whether he was going to survive or get killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. But just stick with the Alispahic question for a moment. When was it, according to your knowledge, that Alispahic tried to get into the village?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when the barriers were set up. After that, I heard something, but like I said, I was not in charge, I couldn't have been in charge, I couldn't be in command of who would be getting in and who wouldn't be getting in. You could be asking the commanders, Zuka and others, who set those things up and who were there to see who could get in and who were preventing other people from getting in. You better ask them. But as far as I'm concerned, I really couldn't tell you much about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When that line-up took place, where were the troops of the Handzar Division?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the line-up -- of the 9th or you mean our unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I mean the line-up that was done by Ramiz Delalic.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then you could ask it a little bit differently. Ramiz lined up his men, the ones that he had. He was not in charge of the Handzar Division. You should have tried at that time to line up that unit. It was mostly Albanians who were members of that unit at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, so what? What's the importance of that?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's the importance of that? The word itself will tell you. We had nothing to do with them. The "Handzar Division," that word should signify something to you. Plus the fact that it was made up of Albanians. This was something quite apart. And they were up at the entrance over there where the checkpoint was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So is it your position -- just perhaps I'll ask you this generally. Is it your position that perhaps the killings were done by men of the 2nd Independent Battalion or the Handzar Division or even Cedo's Wolves?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to that. The witness can give evidence of what he saw or what he -- what he's heard, if it's relevant to the proceedings. But his general opinion as to what may or may not have occurred, in my respectful submission, is irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Rather than have a controversy, I'll just ask him that question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you hear that the men of the Handzar of Cedo's Wolves and of Solakovic's unit may have participated in the killings?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm any of that. Anybody could have done that, in my opinion. Even the inmates could have done it. Who knows who killed who there. Those who actually committed that act probably know it best.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. One thing you can say is that you were shocked and surprised to hear what had happened; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. When I saw those kids, I had left behind two children of that very same age back in Sarajevo, and they were exposed to thousands of shells every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Just excuse me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Arnautovic, you've been very patient. I've just got perhaps five more minutes of questioning and then I've finished with my questions. You indicated that on the night of the 10th, the fighters went walking off on the long route to Dreznica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were going out to an operation or an action and they were walking to Dreznica. They went down along the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But your account is that the unit returned back to Sarajevo on the 12th or the 13th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unit returned on the 12th to the 13th, and I remember that because I was wondering if I would be back there or not for my birthday. And I returned to Sarajevo on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So you were back for your birthday; yes?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you can remember seeing Sefer Halilovic, Zuka, and the journalist Sevko Hodzic in the village of Grabovica on the occasion when your photograph was taken; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And as far as you know, when did the battle that the 9th Brigade soldiers were going to fight in actually commence in the Vrdi area or the Dreznica area generally?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I remember I wasn't there. I think that it started around the 18th -- the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Did you know whether or not Zuka, Zulfikar Alispago issued a combat order named "Defence of people's rights" on the 11th of September, 1993? Did you know about that order or not?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There was an order for our unit to go to Dreznica and then from there to go to Vrdi, something like that. I don't know the exact name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Arnautovic, when you were arrested on the 26th of October, 1993 during the Operation Trebevic II, you were threatened by the people who arrested you with being skinned alive, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That they would execute me and all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And they mistreated -- I'm not going to go into the details, but it's safe to say they mistreated you in a number of ways on that occasion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the night in several ways. During the night, at 3.00 in the morning, they even tried to kill me from the back, and the military police officer who had brought me in, he knew he because I helped him during the war with cigarettes in the hospital. But there was allegedly an attempt to kill me from the back while apparently attempting to run away. That was the idea. This was something that happened on many occasions. They killed many people like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, look, I'll stick to the questions concerning you. But when you were questioned, it was quite obvious to you that the police who questioned you were desperate to find something against Ramiz Delalic. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. They were trying with all their might to find something because some individuals from those corps hated him, because he was a true fighter. He went in front of the men into battle during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And he was very loyal to you -- to his -- to his fighters; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was just a good man.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you need anything though, perhaps it would be better to ask him. You can call him and then he would probably be able to give you a better explanation about certain things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I've only got a couple more questions for you. The last -- one question is that when you were -- when you were questioned by those police officers -- perhaps I should ask you: Do you know their names, the ones who questioned you?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say. I don't remember the names. I can just maybe call them by one name. I don't know. I have no words for the conduct of those people. Because these people were in cellars while we were waging battles. I have no words to describe them. The best thing I can say is that they are just cattle. I apologise to this court. And they are still calling me in Sarajevo, making phone calls and everything, and all I can say about them is that they are just a bunch of rednecks, and I hope the Court will excuse me for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Arnautovic, those same people pressed you with some questions about Sefer Halilovic as well, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding the events in Grabovica, there were the least number of questions. More questions were about some sort of personal interests of theirs, including Sefer's. Because they were these high-ranking military officers there also who hate Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you know their names?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually these high-ranking ones, Rasim Delic, and these other ones who were ministers. It's known how they hated him. He's from Sandzak; that's one reason. And then it went from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And it was famous and well known that there was political rivalry and dislike between Sefer Halilovic and Bakir Alispahic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know the situation in Sarajevo, Sefer Halilovic at that time, as far as I know, was an honest honourable man, in Sarajevo. I have other things about Bakir Alispahic, maybe some criminal acts, he had been brought in, detained before. So he is a sort of bad apple, where in a basket of apples there are bound to be some rotten apples, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The last question is this --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sometime after all of these events, do you recall receiving a presidential pardon authorised by an individual named Mr. Mujezinovic but effectively emanating from the president, Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, they didn't have any proof against me, and then in the meantime there was this pardon issued by the Presidency that Alija Izetbegovic passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And do you recall when you got that pardon?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was released from prison earlier because they didn't have anything, and then the pardon was declared after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Arnautovic, thank you for your patience. Thank you, Your Honours. Those are the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll take a break and we'll resume at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any redirect, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. I won't be very long. Before I start, I just wish to correct something. In an earlier submission, I believe I probably inadvertently misled the Trial Chamber when I referred to the statement to the cantonal court as being unsigned. I didn't have it in front of me. I wasn't in fact thinking of the statement my learned friend Mr. Morrissey was cross-examining the witness on, which was the statement to the military -- the state security sector of 1993, not 1998. So I just wish to correct the record there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Arnautovic, Mr. Morrissey asked you some questions yesterday about the behaviour of Celo's soldiers, and you told the Trial Chamber that Celo wouldn't let his soldiers drink or go into battle drunk. Now, Celo, Ramiz Delalic, is he a religious man?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And does he have religious views about drink or alcohol?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also share that. Our faith does not permit us to take alcohol, drugs, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey also asked you about civilians digging trenches at the front lines in Sarajevo in 1993 before you went to Grabovica. My question is this: Did you when you were there in Sarajevo in -- up to September 1993 hear of any reports of civilians involuntarily digging trenches -- sorry, digging trenches at the front line after having been taken there by members of the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's -- in the circumstances of this case, the question on its face is not -- not objectionable, but there are various parts of the 1st Corps, and it really ought to be clarified, given the nature of what my learned friend is entitled to ask about. And there's a legitimate purpose behind the questions he's asking. It really ought to be clarified which units he's talking about. "The 1st Corps" is too broad given the nature of the things before the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe there will be some follow-up questions to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Arnautovic, a deliberately general question about the 1st Corps, if you heard any reports about civilians being taken involuntarily to the front line to dig trenches by units within the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which units are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were brigades that would pick up smugglers or profiteers usually.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you able to say which brigades within the 1st Corps they were?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was talk around Sarajevo that the 10th had a bit of that, taking people for digging.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You mean the 10th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I think the 10th was a mountain brigade, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey also asked you about the arrival of soldiers in Grabovica on the 8th of September and whether it was trucks or buses. Were you aware of any other truckloads or bus loads of soldiers from any units from anywhere arriving in Grabovica on the 8th of September, apart from your own?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. As far as I can recall, I think it was just us. Because I heard that the 10th was billeted in Jablanica later, a number of them, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey today asked you about the leadership of the -- of your unit, the 9th, when you travelled from Grabovica -- sorry, from Sarajevo to Grabovica on the 7th and 8th of September, 1993. In cross-examination, you referred to a problem with the police at a place called Pazaric on the way to Grabovica on the night of the 7th or 8th of September 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, even before the question is asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: -- I'm going to object to it. That wasn't this -- I don't have the line number, but you'll recall me objecting to this matter in evidence in chief when my learned friend attempted to raise it. We object to it as irrelevant, and should we need to go any further, we'll object to it on another ground as well. But at this stage it's the same objection, same objection really as was raised on the last occasion. It's not relevant to Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the question is whether you asked this question or not in your cross-examination. If you asked this question in your cross-examination, I believe that the Prosecution is entitled to re-examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, if you analyse -- it's at line 19, Your Honour, of the ever-moving page. The more I talk, the less you're going to be able to see it. I direct the Court to look at that line 19 briefly, and then I'll make my submission. Now, you'll see there that the question that's -- that's said to ground Mr. Re's re-examination relates to the leadership. But what he's really asking about at the bottom is something quite different. It's about the -- the incident at Pazaric. So although it was a good try, in my submission it doesn't arise out of cross-examination and I object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If Your Honour could hear me, the question my learned friend Mr. Morrissey asked was at page 34 of yesterday's transcript. He said -- he said, "You drove through the night at Grabovica. Did you go somewhere before you got to Grabovica? Where did you stop en route?" Answer: "We had problems in a place called Pazaric." Moving on from there, "Where did you stop?" That was the passage in relation to Pazaric. Mr. Morrissey, my learned friend, cross-examined the witness at some length as to the leadership of the unit. I wish to ask him about who sorted out the problems at Pazaric and why, which goes to leadership issue. That's the basis upon which I put that particular question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, so long as it's related to that leadership issue, you may proceed. I believe that it's just a pre-emptive attack, you know, from the Defence on that very issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's so. But would you mind just hearing me on that question. I haven't had the chance to go into what happened at Pazaric. I haven't -- I've kept away from it deliberately in cross-examination. It's got nothing to do with the case, in our submission, and I didn't deal with it. Now, my learned friend is entitled to ask questions about leadership, but merely mentioning the word "leadership" doesn't make any potential incident relevant. He could ask about Mr. Halilovic's leadership or Zuti's leadership or someone else's leadership in 1997 and it would be about leadership but it wouldn't be relevant to this case. This issue here was not cross-examined on and it's not legitimate, in my submission, for my friend to bring the incident in as a showcase for a discussion about leadership. There are plenty of other issues that -- through which he could make the same point, in my submission, and this one is not one which was cross-examined upon and is not a legitimate incident to be raised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll see, you know, how it goes, you know, to see whether it's relevant to this case or not. Yes. You may proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you of the details about the incident at Pazaric in any detail. You mentioned there was an incident along the way that involved the police.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't not understand whether the witness said yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just please repeat your answer. Was it yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did the problems involving your -- your men, your -- the people you were travelling with and the police get resolved? Who resolved them?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ramiz Delalic went to the police station and the whole thing ended when he left, and then we continued on our way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did Ramiz Delalic of all the people travelling in that convey of 120-odd people, why was he the one who went to the police station and managed to have the whole thing ended?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He went because they knew him. In order to prevent any bigger problems occurring, he went to resolve that. We were an army after all, and regular police -- reserve police - it's not even the real police - should not be in a position to stop us when we're going on the road and to harass us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you consider his role to be when he went to the police station? His role, as opposed to all the other 120-odd people in that convoy.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought that he went to resolve that. There was something wrong there at the very start when you leave for something to happen. The police should have been informed that the soldiers were supposed to pass, that they were on their way to the front. Instead of that, we were stopped and then we were said, "Let's see. Wait for this. Wait for that." Then there were swear words exchanged, curses, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I'm asking you specifically is what your understanding was of Ramiz Delalic's role in why he went to resolve the issue with the police, rather than you or any of the other 120 people.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he was known as a commander. That's why he went to resolve the situation. Nobody knew exactly what the intentions of the police were. You can't really say.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said he was known as a commander, and was that how -- was he recorded as a commander by the 120 people who were in that convoy, including yourself?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew who -- that we could rely on him to prevent problems, to prevent conflicts from breaking out, because none of the fighters understood why we had been stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was he known as a commander to?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was known in Sarajevo and through the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he known as a commander to those in the convoy?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course he was known, because he was the deputy commander of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And was that continuing throughout the journey to Grabovica, that he was -- that he continued to be known as the deputy commander of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, there's a number of -- in fact, I don't object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The whole brigade knew, because it happened before that. That Besirevic came. There was a change. And then he became the deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey also asked you about the statement you made to an -- a Prosecution investigator you called Nikolai and you spoke about some language issues. How would you describe the quality of Investigator Nikolai's Bosnian or attempts at Bosnian?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he couldn't speak Bosnian well. He could speak a dialect of sorts, but it could be understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember - and you answered Mr. Morrissey that there was an interpreter there - whether either Nikolai or the interpreter read the statement in English back to you before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. I know only that I didn't receive any piece of paper and that he put questions to me more than -- more directly than through the interpreter. It was he who spoke to me most in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You also were questioned about a second statement to the cantonal court in 1998, and you told the Trial Chamber that you had no respect for their methods of work. What was it about the way they went about their work that leads you to say you had no respect for their work?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they were all linked. It was a kind of clan. Ismet Dahic, the minister of the police, and the prosecutor's office, the prosecutor, then Bisic something, the judge. Later on they were all chased out and replaced. Some were pensioned off and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just describe how you made the statement, just the -- the making of the statement, what you did and how they took the statement, as briefly as possible.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went there to make that statement, first of all it wasn't clear to me why and what for. I said, "As far as Grabovica goes, I didn't see who did the killing. I didn't see anything. I don't know anything. I told them what Vehbija Karic had said. I told them about it all very briefly. I didn't want to enter into any conversations with them. I just told them what I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you have a lawyer with you when you went there?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, just a typist and the judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you ever given a copy of a statement from that court?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, I just signed and went out the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you read it before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't read it. I just signed and left. Because I was fasting that day. It was Ramadan, and I didn't want to be provoked by someone. I didn't want to become upset and ruin my fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you aware whether the details in that statement are correct or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That goes beyond what's legitimate in re-examination, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think in cross-examination you challenged that statement. You know, you put this statement to the witness, and the -- so the Prosecution is entitled to ask some questions, whether he believes that statement is correct or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I agree with the second part of Your Honour's proposition, and I've said what I have to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want to show you a statement which is a three-page document dated the 3rd of December, 1998. Do you recognise that as the statement taken at the Sarajevo cantonal court on the 3rd of December, 1998?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I see here contains part of what I said, partly, but many things here are unknown to me. I was there very briefly. I said I didn't know who did the killing. I didn't know who did what. I can't point a finger at anyone because I wasn't there at the time. And I told them that very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are all the details in the statement correct or not?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some are correct and some are not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In the interests of time, I don't wish to take the witness right through to statement to ask him what is correct and what is incorrect, unless Your Honours feel that -- that it would assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey also asked you a number of questions about the statement you made on the 7th of -- the statement you made on the 7th of October, 1999 to the Prosecution, and the statement you made about Mr. Karadzic [sic] -- his statement about throwing the Croat civilians in the river and whether it occurred on the 8th or the 9th of September. You remember Mr. Morrissey asking you that earlier?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that he asked me that about what Vehbija Karic said.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The transcript actually says Karadzic at 85:5. It should actually be Karic. My question is: Some 11 and a half years after seeing the events you described, what is the state of your memory as to whether what you saw with Mr. Karic occurred on the 8th or the 9th? That's the first or the second day --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's an objection to that. Your Honour, the questions that I put about that statement, as the Court will recall, did not relate to whether it was on the 8th or the 9th but to the fact that he attributed there to be two visits in that statement by Vehbija Karic. And you'll recall it was said -- what was read to him was a passage that expressed effectively that there'd been an visit on the 8th and then there was another visit the next morning on the 9th. He gave answers about that and he said, well -- words to the effect, I think, "I didn't say anything like that so the statements not right."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think, you know, the Prosecution is just asking about own which date, you know, Mr. Karic, you know, making that statement, because, you know -- you know, the Prosecution is trying to clarify whether it's the first day or the second day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What the question by my learned friend is trying to do is to do the reverse of clarify but trying to create some doubt as to which day it was said. Because the question is: Has he got a good memory about it. And when Your Honour looks at the question, it's really a question about his memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The first part is not proper; you are right on that. But the second part, well, there is some merit there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As to which day it was, I've got no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Arnautovic, are you now able to say with any certainty some 11 and a half years later whether it was on the first or the second day that Mr. Karic --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can already object even though the question is not finished. This question has got the same problem that the last one had. There's an easy way to ask it if he has to ask it: He can say which day did it happen, the 8th or the 9th?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, make a simple question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Arnautovic, was it the first day or the second day of your arrival that Mr. Karic made his comment about throwing Croats into the river?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be precise. In my opinion, what I can conclude and what I can remember is that it was on the second day. I can't be absolutely certain now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just remember those words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge El Mahdi, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] Witness, I have two clarifications I would like to obtain from you. The first has to do with what you said about what happened on the 26th of October, 1993. You said, and I quote in English, "arrested." [Interpretation] I would like to know the following: When you say "we," who was that we? Who were you?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All of the army?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Men from three or four brigades were arrested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And members of the -- of the troops who were in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some who were in Grabovica and also others, a larger number of others were arrested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But you were asked questions about the events that took place in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 26th of October, when we were arrested, there were just a few questions about Grabovica that were asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But do you remember a specific question?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember there were seven or eight of them there and they asked me, "Do you know who did the killings? Who killed those people? Did you see anything? Confess. If you don't confess, you will be shot." Such things happened. But as I really hadn't seen anything, of course I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the same question was -- was the same question put to some of your -- the men who were with you?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, what I saw in prison, yes. Yes, they asked them that. But for the most part, they threatened everyone, saying they would be beaten up, and some were beaten up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
