utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. So -- but if I understand correctly, what you're saying is that those who were arrested on the 26th were men from your units but also members from units that were located in Grabovica. Among others, the 10th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the 10th, a lot of their men were arrested too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And according to you, if you know anything about that -- according to you, were they interrogated also about the incidents that took place in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some individuals who were in the cell with me said they had been asked whether they knew anything about what had happened, whether they knew that someone had killed someone, what they had seen, what they had heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The last question about what you said, if I understand correctly: You said that you were pardoned. You were -- this pardon was granted by a presidential decision, a presidential decree.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was released before that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But had you been found guilty? Because you said you were pardoned, so does it mean that you had been found guilty?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't guilty. I was released because people were in prison and every two or three days they would release one or two of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But why were they in prison? Because of the events that had taken place in Grabovica or for other reasons?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what we were told, we were accused of armed rebellion. I was at home asleep when I was arrested. I couldn't understand what sort of armed rebellion they were talking about. I thought an armed rebellion was when somebody took over the television, broadcasting station, the Presidency, government buildings, and that hadn't happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. My last question: You said about the event that took place when Mr. Karic was present. You said that next to him there were four to five, in English [In English] "People from the corps." [Interpretation] You were not able to identify who these people were. But could you at least tell us what division, what corps, what brigade these people belonged to, according to their insignias, according to their clothing.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only remember vaguely that one of them was nicknamed Zico and that they belonged to the Herzegovina unit. I don't know whether it was a company. And they belonged to that corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What corps? What was the name of that corps?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was the 6th or the 4th Corps. I know there was some argument about that, but they belonged to the Herzegovina part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In other words, you came to the conclusion that these people belonged either to the 6th or to the 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't really understand very well who was in what corps. I know there was a corps there. Whether it was the 4th or the 6th, I can't be sure, but I know that that corps was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judge's questions? I see --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I see none. At this stage are there any documents to tender? I see none. Well, witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. Madam Usher will show you out of the room and all of us wish you a pleasant journey back home. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that the Prosecution has something to say about --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- the application for the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I wish to make an application for protective measures for the witness after the next one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could we go into the private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, good afternoon, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, the witness is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Would you state your name for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Nedzad Mehanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us your age and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: 6th of January, 1969. I'm 37 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I want to go through some of your background, and I'm going to ask you some leading questions so we can go through it quickly. You completed secondary school for mechanical engineering; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you're employed as a caterer?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You're a member of the Muslim ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you're a member of the SDA party in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You have been living in Sarajevo since 1984?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: As you had been born in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You first joined the TO of Sarajevo in 1992, which is the Territorial Defence unit?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You served -- you then served in the Sandzak Brigade, the military police unit?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Sandzak Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And after that, you served in the 3rd Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: In the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you eventually wound up in the 9th Motorised Brigade. Could you tell the Court how you went from the military police unit of the 3rd Mountain Brigade to the 9th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: We moved from the Sandzak to Delalic to the military police. I don't know how many months we spent there. And then the 3rd Mountain Brigade was formed in January 1993. I don't know exactly when. But it was in 1993. I don't know which month that the 3rd and the 7th joined together to become the 9th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Which unit did you serve within the 9th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: In the assault company.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did the assault company members receive any special training?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what was the role of the assault company?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Liberation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where was that located?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: First in Sloga. After that, in the Romanijska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And are these regions within Sarajevo or areas within Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the old town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, how many soldiers were within the 9th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I heard that it was between five to six thousand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us who the commander and deputy commanders were.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Of the brigade or of the assault company?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Of the brigade, sir.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: The commander was Sulejman Imsirovic and the deputy was Ramiz Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, of these five to six thousand soldiers, were some of them involved in criminal activity in the year 1993? And we're talking about prior to going to Herzegovina in September 1993.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't describe it as "criminal activities." These were just individuals like you would have in any army, individuals like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, what type of crimes would be committed by some of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness be asked to approach the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, are you familiar with a soldier named Mustafa Hota?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And was he a member of the 9th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: From 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was Mustafa Hota and the soldiers associated with him involved in criminal activity?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. They were doing something that they weren't -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you recall any problems relating to Mustafa Hota in relation to inciting others to act improperly?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Your Honour, I object to that. Your Honour, I raise an objection to that. There can't be any leading in relation to these matters. I didn't object to leading on the uncontentious things. But I do object to leading from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And the question is not very clear, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you recall any situations where Mustafa Hota incited others to commit criminal activity? Were you aware of any of that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that he was fighting or quarrelling with the police, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know an individual or a soldier named Nihad Vlahovljak?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what was his position?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: He was the platoon commander, a special platoon. I don't know. As part of the 2nd Battalion, but I'm not exactly sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And was the 2nd Battalion subordinated to the 9th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you aware of any criminal activity by Nihad Vlahovljak's unit?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Had you heard - not whether or not you've seen it - had you heard about any criminal activity by that unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Once again -- I'm sorry, I'll just have to stop the witness. Pardon me. Once again, I'll really have to object to that. That question really is so vague and unfocussed in time that it seems to me to be meaningless, for the purposes of these proceedings anyway, and in any event -- well, I just limit my objection to that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you should raise your objections in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The second question is just a follow-up of the first question. First of all they ask whether you are aware of any criminal activities; then have you heard. Now, it's just a follow-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, if that's the way that Your Honour interprets it, then I object on the basis that it's just a repeat in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, since the witness has already answered the first question, so I'll allow it, the witness to answer the second question. Your objection is registered in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Had you heard of his unit being involved in any criminal activity which occurred prior to September 1993?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: I heard, but not the entire unit. Again, I am saying that this was something that was done by individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what type of crimes did you hear that these individuals committed?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: To take some goods from the market, to take it from smugglers. Something like that I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's move on to September 1993. Could you tell us what occurred in relation to first being called to Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. To describe the situation or to go from the beginning or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, could you tell us first where you were in September, during the first week of September in 1993. First, what unit were you in?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: The 9th Motorised, the assault company.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And sometime in September 1993, were you called to line up?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In front of the brigade in Trampina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you tell the Court who was present.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: We heard that and before we lined up -- that we were supposed to go to Herzegovina. We were wearing full combat equipment. We came to the brigade and lined up and then Vahid Karavelic came, the commander of the 1st Corps, and he read out an order to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What did he tell you? Please tell the Court.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: He read the order that -- an order had arrived from the General Staff, I don't know -- for us to go to Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did they explain why you had to go to Herzegovina or did he explain why you had to go to Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: That there was a difficult situation in relation to the 4th Corps there and to liberate Mostar, something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did they state the name of the operation that was to take place?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Neretva 93.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you who your commander would be when you got to Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As soon as we crossed the pista, it would be Zulfikar Alispago. We would be under his command.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What did you do after they finished speaking to you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: We got ready, went to the tunnel, passed through the tunnel. It rained heavily that night, so the trucks had not arrived. Then we returned once again to the town. And then on the second night, we actually left. I think it was the 7th.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what was your destination when you left?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Igman, Pazaric, Konjic, back to Bradina, and then from Bradina to Donja Jablanica, and from Donja Jablanica to Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you in fact follow that route and arrive at Donja Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you arrive there on the same day as you left or on the following day?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: We arrived at Donja Jablanica at 11.15, as far as I can recall, near Zuka's base.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And was that on the 7th of September, the same day you left, or on the following day?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: The 8th of September. I think that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you said -- did you have with you a diary or did you maintain a diary or keep any records of this travel?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you have a watch?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you arrived at Zuka's base and -- at Donja Jablanica. Did you stay there very long?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: 15 or 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where did you go from there?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Two, three, four -- I don't know exactly how many. They showed us the way and took us to Grabovica. These were Zuka's logistics men.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When you said, "They showed us the way," do you mean they escorted you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were in the first truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, how long of a ride is it from Donja Jablanica to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: About 20 minutes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When you arrived, where did they bring you in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: That's the only way to Grabovica, so it's the road that goes in the direction of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Where -- within Grabovica, where did they leave you off, you and the other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: On the right bank in that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did they bring you directly to houses or did they leave you somewhere?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: No. In front of one house, in the front yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How many people were left in front of -- in the front yard of one house?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: About 50 of us. That's how many there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How long did you remain there?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Then they told us to go into the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How did you wind up in a house? Did you just walk around and find one, or did someone bring you to one?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: I was taken to one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Who took you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: The logistics persons who came with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, could you describe the house that they brought you to.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you please describe it to the Judges.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: It was an old house more or less consisting of a ground floor and an attic. It was the first on the right-hand side at the entrance to Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Who else stayed in that house?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: I came there towards evening, at about 5.00 or 6.00, with a companion of mine. His name was Haris. When we got there, Crni, Regan and Suljo were already in the house. There were five of us altogether in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you given any food or did you have to go out and find your own food?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: The first place that they took us, that's where they brought the food, to that front yard. Then everybody would take the food and eat it in the houses where they were billeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, after you arrived -- actually, when you say "they brought the food," who is "they"? Who were the persons who provided the food?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly their names. They were logistics people from Zuka's units, people who were in charge of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did you stay very long at that house?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Perhaps half an hour to an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, what did you do after that one half hour to an hour later?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: I went to Jablanica with a friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Haris Salihovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Why did you go to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: I had a lot of friends there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Had you ever been there previously?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Had you ever worked with their defence, their soldiers or their defence plan -- their defence unit?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When the war with the Croats began, on the 23rd of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: I just happened to be in Jablanica. There was some order regarding uniforms and weapons. I just happened to be there when the war with the Croats broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you assist them in any way?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were about 20 men there that I assembled, because war hadn't broken out there yet, I assembled about 20 men and we took part in the defence together with Commander Kovacevic of the 44th Mountain. I think that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how long did you plan to stay in Jablanica that night that you left Grabovica and went to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Since the accommodation in Grabovica was bad and I had accommodation in Jablanica, I thought that I would spend every night there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did you spend that night, which would have been the 8th of September, 1993, in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you return to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: The next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Approximately what time did you return? What time of the day?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC
utterances.text: Around 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it would be a good time to break here before we start the next day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, witness, I'm afraid that you have to stay here for another night. And as I did to other witnesses, that I have to warn you you are still under the oath, so do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, completely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So we'll see you tomorrow afternoon. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
